title: Where the keyboard lands after a keyboard close is a second pending-close record, settled by polling each frame
why: The five stations are there as cited (TabPicks::close_had_keyboard, MarkdownApp::keyboard_closing, keyboard_landing, Landing, TabLabel::takes_keyboard). The remedy is sound by reading, with one correction: request_close_tab has two production callers (tabs/mod.rs:324, tab_bar/mod.rs:198) and four in tests (explorer_panel/tests.rs:290, :315; close_prompt/tests.rs:137, :155), and close_prompt/tests.rs:57 builds Goal::Tab(1), so keep request_close_tab(index) and add a second entry for the keyboard. Carrying the flag in the goal also survives the overwrite question of PR 21 for free. Not run: the focus request made in the frame the modal is still the top layer.
observable: none intended; the ring appears one frame earlier
size: 4 files (tab_bar, close_prompt, app/mod.rs, startup), about 70 lines removed and 30 added; the new-tab button needs a fixed id
guards: tests/reader/keyboard_focus.rs (7 tests on closing from the keyboard) name none of the removed items and should pass unchanged; src/app/close_prompt/tests.rs:57 changes to the struct variant. No proof or TSV row. tab_bar/mod.rs changes by more than 100 lines in total, so split it into two commits.

title: Tab::id names the document and Tab::serial the tab, and revealed_tab still keys on place and document
why: Real: revealed_tab is Option<(usize, egui::Id)> (app/mod.rs:81) built at tab_bar/mod.rs:96, twenty lines from the serial. The review's 'no observable change with (serial, document_id)' is wrong: today the key holds the place, so closing a tab to the left of the front tab moves the front tab's place and scrolls it back into the strip; keyed by serial that reveal is gone. No test pins it. The rename of Tab::id is mechanical (content/mod.rs:168, :260; outline/spy/mod.rs:93; tab_bar/mod.rs:96; tab/mod.rs).
observable: With the serial key, the strip no longer scrolls back to the front tab when a tab to its left is closed.
diff:
sketch, not compiled
- pub(crate) id: egui::Id,
+ pub(crate) document_id: egui::Id,
- revealed_tab: Option<(usize, egui::Id)>,
+ revealed_tab: Option<(u64, egui::Id)>,   // only with the behaviour change accepted
size: rename: 4 files, about 8 mentions. Key change: 2 files, 3 lines
guards: src/app/tab_bar/tests.rs a_tab_that_comes_to_the_front, a_tab_that_takes_the_place_of_a_closed_one, a_second_tab_on_the_same_document, the_strip_stays_where_the_reader_scrolled_it pass under either key. PR 27 conflicts textually with PR 23 in src/tab/mod.rs and tab_bar/mod.rs.

title: The home page's buttons and the contents sidebar's fold control take the keyboard and draw no focus ring
why: Both are laid out with ui.interact(.., Sense::click()), which is focusable, and neither calls chrome::focus_ring (welcome/mod.rs:232-244, outline/mod.rs:251-265). The Tab key reaches each of them and no ring is painted. The 'same ten lines' claim is loose: more_button and quiet_button share the interact, the name and the hover wash but paint different things, so one call to focus_ring at each site is the smaller fix.
observable: The Tab key stops on Open File…, Open Folder… and on each fold chevron with nothing on screen showing where the keyboard is.
size: 2 files, 2 lines, plus 2 reader tests in tests/reader/keyboard_focus.rs
guards: No test pins the lack of a ring. tests/reader/keyboard_focus.rs has assert_ring_follows_the_keyboard to reuse.
repro: reproduced: `assertion left == right failed: Open File…, focused  left: None  right: Some(#B25E28)` and the same for `fold, focused`; tab_to reached both controls

Neither reads has_focus. The theme swatches do react to focus (appearance/mod.rs:54), with a darker edge and no ring.

title: A held key is defended against twice, once by where the keyboard lands and once by deleting repeats in the prompt
why: The filter is at close_prompt/mod.rs:249. The remedy (give Save the keyboard only once the key is up, delete the filter) is unsafe next to PR 21: while the key is held the focus stays on the first button, and on the overwrite question the first button is Overwrite, so every repeat presses it (see 21-N1, which shows the same mechanism in one frame). The filter is what protects the second question from repeats once both PRs are merged.
observable: With the remedy, Save takes the keyboard on key release, not on press.
guards: tests/reader/keyboard_focus.rs a_key_held_down_on_the_close_button_of_unsaved_edits_asks_and_answers_nothing. PR 21 renames focus_save to focus_due on the same line: a textual conflict either way.

options.cost: Nothing; 13 lines and a queue edit in a render function stay, and they also cover the overwrite question.

options.name: Replace it with focus on key release
options.cost: 15 lines fewer, but only safe after 21-N1 is fixed; Save takes the keyboard later; one test to re-check by running.
